title: Design System: Otto 在线编舞台

bed.purpose: Page ground and the left panel's stock. The field the slides lie on; roughly half the visible surface.

carbon.purpose: The stage and the rack — everything the robot is watched on, plus inputs and the code strip.

ivory.purpose: The reversed surface: the selected frame, the modal sheet, a hovered neutral button.

vermilion.purpose: The armed state: osc labels, the playing frame edge, warnings, focus rings, danger hover. Never a background for body text.

bottle.purpose: The confirmed connection: one 8px dot, plus the status word when connected (#9FD3B6 at 10.41:1 on carbon).

ui.purpose: Every label, value and heading in the interface, set in Archivo Narrow (embedded base64 woff2, latin subset, 400/700). Measured 10x'M' at 13px = 88.80px; the Arial fallback would be 108.30px.

ui-mobile.purpose: The same single size raised for a phone held at arm's length.

data.purpose: The sequence JSON. A different substance from a label, so it gets the mono stack at 11.5px.

data-inline.purpose: Angle pairs inside frame cards and the refdes chips beside each axis name.

shadows.name: bed-lip-offset
shadows.purpose: The only depth cue: a sheet sitting on the bed casts a 2px hard edge in the bed's lip tone. No blur, no spread.

shadows.name: slab-offset
shadows.purpose: The carbon slabs' hard edge against the bed.

shadows.name: sheet-inner-light
shadows.purpose: One hairline of light on the goldenrod panel's top edge so the stock reads as paper, not as a fill.

shadows.name: playing-edge
shadows.purpose: The frame being previewed. An edge, not a glow.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Two-tone, because one colour cannot survive three grounds: carbon halo 6.30:1 on goldenrod, ivory ring 14.62:1 on carbon. Single vermilion measured only 1.79:1 on the bed.

motion.name: toast-in
motion.purpose: The only element that moves on its own.

gradients.name: stage-light-pool
gradients.purpose: The lamp behind the robot. Light, not elevation — the only soft gradient in the interface.

gradients.name: servo-scale
gradients.value: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(28,25,19,.45) 0 1px, transparent 1px 15px) over a 1px rule
gradients.purpose: A graduation scale for 0–180°, one tick every 15°. Functional measurement, not decoration.

gradients.name: ruler-scale
gradients.purpose: The acetate ruler's graduation under the stage; the playhead chip rides it.

gradients.name: bed-lamp
gradients.purpose: The same lamp that lights the stage falls on the bed: a 4% value lift so the goldenrod reads as lit paper rather than flat paint.

breakpoints.name: desk-narrow
breakpoints.note: Columns tighten, bed gutters drop to 10px.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.note: One stack, stage first via order:-1; page scrolls; the pose library stops scrolling internally.

breakpoints.name: handheld
breakpoints.note: Type 13→15px, bed margin 8px, 42px touch targets, frame actions wrap to their own row.

components.name: Section Head
components.description: Uppercase tracked title with a right-aligned micro tag, separated by a single hairline. No background, no box.

components.name: Servo Row
components.description: One axis: name, reversed mono key chip, value, ticked track with a 3px bar thumb, range description. Right-side servos carry the vermilion-deep value so side is legible without a second colour.
components.html:
90°
0内收 / 90中立 / 180外展

components.name: Frame Card
components.description: A slide in the rack. A sheared ticket carries the number and the type; the body carries one line of mono angle pairs and a meta line whose actions sit flush right. Selection reverses the whole card to ivory.
components.html:
#1姿态
ll90rl90
v=800ms · d=100ms
components.css: .frame{display:grid;grid-template-columns:54px minmax(0,1fr);margin-bottom:5px;cursor:pointer;background:#2C3A40;color:#F2EAD6;border:1px solid rgba(242,234,214,.12);border-left:0}.frame .ticket{display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center;padding:4px 11px 4px 6px;white-space:nowrap;background:rgba(242,234,214,.1);border-right:1px solid rgba(242,234,214,.14);clip-path:polygon(0 0,100% 0,calc(100% - 8px) 100%,0 100%)}.frame .ticket b{font-family:'Cascadia Mono',Consolas,monospace;font-weight:500}.frame .ticket span{letter-spacing:.1em;color:#CFC4A8}.frame .ticket span.osc{color:#EE8A6A}.frame.active{background:#F2EAD6;color:#1C1913;border-color:#F2EAD6}.frame.active .ticket{background:#1C1913;border-right-color:#1C1913}.frame.active .ticket b,.frame.active .ticket span{color:#C8912C}.frame.playing{box-shadow:inset 3px 0 0 #C4442B}.frame-angles{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:9px;font-family:'Cascadia Mono',Consolas,monospace}.frame-angles b{color:#B4A98D;font-weight:400;margin-right:2px}.frame.active .frame-angles b{color:rgba(28,25,19,.6)}.frame-meta{font-family:'Cascadia Mono',Consolas,monospace;color:#B4A98D}.frame.active .frame-meta{color:rgba(28,25,19,.62)}

components.name: Tick Rail
components.description: A 16px index column beside the rack: one tick per frame, the current one wider and vermilion. It shows the extent of the sequence, not a proportional timeline.

components.name: Ruler + Playhead
components.description: A 26px graduated strip under the stage. The playhead chip is the only goldenrod fill inside the carbon stage.
components.css: .ruler{height:26px;display:flex;align-items:center;border-top:1px solid rgba(242,234,214,.14);border-bottom:1px solid rgba(242,234,214,.14);background:repeating-linear-gradient(90deg,rgba(242,234,214,.34) 0 1px,transparent 1px 50px) left bottom/100% 9px no-repeat,repeating-linear-gradient(90deg,rgba(242,234,214,.18) 0 1px,transparent 1px 10px) left bottom/100% 4px no-repeat}.playhead{margin:5px 0 5px auto;padding:0 7px;font-family:'Cascadia Mono',Consolas,monospace;color:#1C1913;background:#C8912C;line-height:16px}

narrative.northStar: 灯台上的斜架幻灯片 — The Lit Slide Rack
narrative.overview:
The tool is a 1971 pocket timetable read as a raked rack of tinted glass slides lying on a lit goldenrod bed. The bed is the field; three sheets sit on it — goldenrod stock holding the six axes, a carbon stage holding the robot, a carbon rack holding the frames. A frame joins the show by sliding into the rack, and its ticket is the thing you read.

The system is narrow on purpose. One type size; rank comes from weight, case, tracking, reversal and rule. One radius: zero. No elevation, no icon set, no gradient used as surface treatment. Every colour names a job — bed, ground, glass, reversal, armed, confirmed — and a colour that cannot name its job is decoration and does not ship.

The point of the world is that the old look (three dark panels, blue accents) could have belonged to any of ten thousand tools. This one belongs to a place: a departure hall, a printer's bench, a sheet of stock under a lamp.
keyCharacteristics: Goldenrod bed carrying roughly half the surface, visible around every panel as a field
Rank by weight, case, tracking, reversal and rule — never by size
Frame tickets sheared 8px on one axis so the rack reads as a stack of slides
Drawn scales: a ticked slider track and a graduated ruler
Square corners and 1px rules everywhere; a 2px hard offset is the only depth
Vermilion as an edge and a label colour, never behind body text

rules.name: The Bed Is Visible Rule
rules.body: Every panel is a sheet on the bed, so the bed must remain visible around and between panels. A layout that lets panels touch the viewport edge has turned the gold into a background fill and broken the world.

rules.name: One Size Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one type size, 13px (15px below 600px). Hierarchy is spent on weight, case, tracking, reversal and rule. Adding a second size is the fastest way to make this interface look like the generic tool it replaced.

rules.name: Named Job Rule
rules.body: Six hues, six jobs: gold is the bed, carbon is the ground, slate is glass, ivory is reversal, vermilion is armed, bottle green is confirmed. A colour without a job is decoration.

rules.name: Solid Ink Rule
rules.body: Text on goldenrod uses solid ink (#1C1913 primary, #3A2C08 secondary), never an alpha tint. Alpha over a saturated ground cannot hold AA at any comfortable lightness.

rules.name: Rake Rule
rules.body: The ticket shear is 8px on the right edge, identical at every card height, aligned on a common axis, and never applied to text. It is the one recurring form in the system.

rules.name: No Elevation Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats and nothing has a blur. Depth is which sheet is on top, marked by a 1px lip and a 2px hard offset in the bed's lip colour.

rules.name: No Side Stripe Rule
rules.body: State is a filled ticket, a reversed sheet, or a drawn rule. An accent bar down one edge of a card or a toast is the generic pattern this world is trying to escape.

rules.name: Instrument Rule
rules.body: A drawn instrument must print real data. The playhead shows the true frame count at rest, the ruler cursor sits at activeFrame/(n-1), and each rail tick is drawn by its own card so it cannot drift.

dos: Keep the goldenrod bed visible around and between panels
Spend rank on weight, case, tracking, reversal and rule first
Draw a scale whenever a number has a range
Give the selected frame the ivory reversal and nothing else
Keep the six axes fixed while the pose library scrolls under them
Use the mono stack only for machine output and inline axis tokens
donts: Add a second type size for hierarchy
Round a corner, lift a card, or add a blurred shadow
Let frame cards drift apart into floating cards
Use a gradient as surface decoration
Reintroduce an icon set — labels are the icons
Use an alpha tint for text on goldenrod
